messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Runtime OOM burst detected in infer-prod-us-west. 48/64 GPUs reporting high paging. Severity: Sev2. Link: https://ops.redwood/p/4921234567
sam-oncall: Ack. I'm on it. Starting triage — gathering logs and customer impact.
maria-rt: Noted, saw errors in metrics: sustained GPU alloc failures around 13:12 UTC. Queueing traces.
sam-oncall: Customer impact: two production customers reported increased latency and 502s; routing fallback triggered for some requests. We've opened a bridge: #incident-4921234567-bridge
incident-bot: Attachments: stack-trace snippets and alert graph uploaded to thread.
sam-oncall: Quick telemetry dump:
```
GPU stats (13:11-13:15 UTC):
node01-gpu0 free: 120MB -> 8MB
node01-gpu0 paged: yes
node03-gpu1 free: 200MB -> 16MB
KV cache hitrate dropped 68% -> 42%
p50 latency: 180ms -> 420ms
```
jin-sre: That's severe fragmentation. Any batch size changes in the last deploy?
nate-eng: No config deploys in last 24h, but traffic spike from model-x rollouts at 13:09 UTC.
maria-rt: Hypothesis A: KV cache thrash + sudden traffic spike caused sustained allocations and page-walks. Hypothesis B: A regressed mem leak in model-x serving path.
sam-oncall: Actions: 1) Temporarily reduce batch_size for model-x on infer pool to 1. 2) Enable per-request kvcache-evict window to reclaim stale entries. 3) If still high, scale out by spinning warm instances.
ops-bridge: On it. Applying batch_size override now.
ops-bridge: Applied patch:
```
kubectl patch deploy infer-model-x -n prod --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/0/value","value":"1"}]'
```
lisa-support: Noted — notifying impacted customers: CS will send update: "We are investigating memory pressure affecting inference latency; temporary mitigations applied." :email:
sam-oncall: After batch_size=1, telemetry (13:18 UTC):
```
GPU free: node01-gpu0 8MB -> 42MB
KV cache hitrate: 42% -> 58%
p50 latency: 420ms -> 220ms
OOM events: declined from 17 -> 2 per min
```
jin-sre: Improvement visible. Need to capture longer timeline and logs for RCA. Please collect `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` and runtime heap profiles from affected pods.
maria-rt: I'm pulling heap and KV traces now. Uploading shard logs to /artifacts/4921234567/
nate-eng: I'll create a quick smoke to confirm model-x isn't misallocating with current input shapes.
sam-oncall: Also recommend we run a controlled batch-size ramp test to see frag threshold. Add to action items.
ops-bridge: Added runbook note: "If fragmentation recurs after scaling, consider forced kvcache-compact and rolling restart of hot nodes."
jin-sre: Hypotheses tracker:
- H1: KV cache thrash (evidence: hitrate drop and recovery after evict)
- H2: Fragmentation due to large allocation patterns from batch spike (evidence: GPU free low during spike)
- H3: Model allocation regression (low priority, no deploys)
maria-rt: Tagging logs: artefact ids: logs-node01-13-11, nvprof-node01-13-12, kvstats-13-10-13-20
sam-oncall: Next: schedule RCA doc and timeline. I've started a timeline note in docs/rca/4921234567.md and will paste raw timelines here.
ops-bridge: Customer impact update posted to CS channel. Customers A & B saw 30-50% latency increase; rolling fallback served 15% of requests.
lisa-support: CS update sent. We'll escalate to account owners for customers with SLAs.
nate-eng: One more datapoint: model-x memory map shows many small allocations (8-32KB) leading to free list fragmentation; may need allocator tuning.
jin-sre: Plan for post-incident: 1) Re-run workload in staging with same traffic spike, 2) Evaluate KV cache LRU window and size, 3) Add telemetry alert to detect fragmentation patterns earlier.
sam-oncall: Closing bridge in 30m unless we see reversion. Keeping thread open for RCA notes.
incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated. Closure will be logged after RCA doc and timeline attached.
